title: Jesus Loves Me
description: Jesus Loves Me in Tonic Solfa, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, the verses and refrain, and a piano. A first song for children's choirs.
about: Anna Bartlett Warner wrote the words as a poem in Say and Seal (1860), a novel she wrote with her sister Susan. William Bradbury set it to music and added the refrain 'Yes, Jesus loves me' in 1862.
The tune uses only five different solfa notes (d r m s l) and moves mostly by step, which makes it a good first song for children learning to sing from solfa.
underlay: Je-sus loves me! this I know, For the Bi-ble tells me so; Lit-tle ones to Him be-long; They are weak, but He is strong. Yes, Je-sus loves me! Yes, Je-sus loves me! Yes, Je-sus loves me! The Bi-ble tells me so.

lines: Jesus loves me! this I know,
For the Bible tells me so;
Little ones to Him belong;
They are weak, but He is strong.

verses.label: Refrain
lines: Yes, Jesus loves me!
Yes, Jesus loves me!
Yes, Jesus loves me!
The Bible tells me so.
Jesus loves me! He who died
Heaven’s gate to open wide;
He will wash away my sin,
Let His little child come in.
Jesus loves me! loves me still,
Though I’m very weak and ill;
From His shining throne on high
Comes to watch me where I lie.
Jesus loves me! He will stay
Close beside me all the way;
If I love Him, when I die
He will take me home on high.
